question:
A group of astrophysicists proposes a theoretical fusion reaction in a newly discovered star where three identical nuclei of an unknown light element $X$ ($^4_2X$) fuse simultaneously to form a single nucleus of element $Y$ ($^{12}_6Y$). Given the atomic masses: $m(^4_2X) = 4.0026 \text{ u}$ and $m(^{12}_6Y) = 12.0000 \text{ u}$ (where $1 \text{ u} = 931.5 \text{ MeV/c}^2$). Answer the following: 

(a) Calculate the $Q$-value of this reaction. 

(b) Justify why it is practically impossible to observe this reaction occurring spontaneously at room temperature on Earth. 

(c) Describe the qualitative shift on the Binding Energy per nucleon ($E_{bn}$) curve for the stellar core during this process.

options.A: (a) $+7.27 \text{ MeV}$ (b) Prevented by strong electrostatic Coulomb repulsion between the positively charged nuclei (c) The core's matter shifts from a region of lower $E_{bn}$ to a higher $E_{bn}$ peak.
options.B: (a) $-7.27 \text{ MeV}$ (b) Prevented by the mass defect which absorbs ambient heat (c) The core's matter shifts from a region of higher $E_{bn}$ to a lower $E_{bn}$ valley.
options.C: (a) $+2.42 \text{ MeV}$ (b) Prevented by the short range of the strong nuclear force at low temperatures (c) The core's matter remains at a constant $E_{bn}$ plateau.
options.D: (a) $+7.27 \text{ MeV}$ (b) Prevented because element $X$ is already at the peak of the stability curve (c) The core's matter shifts to a lower $E_{bn}$ peak.
